title: A plaint is the document by which a civil suit is instituted (Order VII CPC)

content.overview: A plaint is the pleading by which a civil suit is instituted under Order VII of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Order VII Rule 1 requires the name of the court, the parties' names and addresses, facts constituting the cause of action and when it arose, facts showing jurisdiction, the relief claimed, and, where the suit is for recovery of money, a statement of its value. Rule 11 lists rejection: no cause of action, relief undervalued and not corrected, insufficiently stamped and not supplied, suit barred by law, or the plaint not filed in duplicate, or non-compliance with Rule 9. The plaint is not a written statement and not an execution petition.
content.short: A plaint is the document by which a civil suit is instituted (Order VII CPC). It must contain particulars of parties, cause of action, facts showing jurisdiction, relief claimed, and valuation. Missing mandatory particulars can lead to rejection under Order VII Rule 11.
content.detailed:
Order VII — key contents of a plaint (exam skeleton)

1. Name of the court
2. Name, description and place of residence of plaintiff
3. Name, description and place of residence of defendant (so far as known)
4. Where plaintiff/defendant is a minor or person of unsound mind — statement to that effect
5. Facts constituting the cause of action and when it arose
6. Facts showing that the court has jurisdiction
7. Relief which the plaintiff claims
8. Where the plaintiff has allowed a set-off or relinquished a portion of claim — statement of that amount
9. Statement of the value of the subject-matter for jurisdiction and court-fees

Rejection of plaint (Order VII Rule 11) — high-yield
Plaint shall be rejected where, inter alia:
• It does not disclose a cause of action
• Relief claimed is undervalued and plaintiff fails to correct
• Plaint is insufficiently stamped and plaintiff fails to supply
• Suit appears barred by law from the statement in the plaint

Exam tip: AIBE tests particulars and Order VII Rule 11 grounds more than long drafting templates.

enhancement.definition: A plaint is the Order VII pleading that institutes a civil suit and states the court, parties, cause of action, jurisdiction and relief.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The suit begins with the plaint. Facts must disclose a cause of action and a court that has jurisdiction. Evidence and legal argument are not a substitute for those particulars.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order VII Rules 1 and 11. Limitation is pleaded as a fact; the Limitation Act bar is applied by the court under section 3 of that Act.
essentialIngredients: Facts of the cause of action and its date
Facts showing territorial, pecuniary and subject-matter jurisdiction
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Rule 1 is a checklist. The cause of action is the bundle of facts the plaintiff must prove, with the date it arose, because limitation and jurisdiction often turn on that date. Jurisdiction is pleaded in facts: where the defendant resides or works for gain, or where the cause of action arose, in whole or in part. The prayer asks for a decree in a form the court can pass. A money suit states the amount. Order VII Rule 11 is the rejection list and should be used as a drafting control: if the facts, even if true, show no cause of action or a bar of law, the plaint is vulnerable. Rejection is not a dismissal after trial. Valuation and court-fee follow the local Court-fees Act and are not given a number here.
examples: A seller pleads the contract, the place of delivery, the invoice date, non-payment, and the defendant's residence, and claims the price.
A plaint says only that the defendant is liable, with no date or facts. Rule 11(a) is the risk.
A decree is already passed. The next document is an execution petition, not a second plaint.
enhancement.problemApplication: Check Rule 1 item by item, then ask whether Rule 11 is attracted on the face of the draft. Do not add evidence as a paragraph of facts.
distinctions: Rejection under Rule 11 vs dismissal after trial
Facts constituting the cause of action vs evidence

keyTakeaways: Order VII Rule 1 is the particulars list.
Plead facts and the date of the cause of action.
Rule 11 is rejection, not a trial result.
Court-fee figures come from the local Act, not from this note.

verification.note: Order VII text only. No case citation. Local court-fee amounts not invented.

content.study: Plead facts, not evidence. Show jurisdiction and limitation in the facts. Claim a specific relief. A missing cause of action or a suit barred on the face of the plaint is a Rule 11 problem.
